issues.description: Class name in code does not match PR title / module-level docs (AWSAgentCoreProcessor vs AWSBedrockAgentCoreProcessor)
issues.detail: The PR title and AWS service name reference 'AWSBedrockAgentCoreProcessor', but the class is named 'AWSAgentCoreProcessor'. The module docstring at the top of agent_core.py also says 'AWSAgentCoreProcessor'. Public API naming should be locked in before merge because renaming later is a breaking change for users following the example PR.

issues.description: Public constructor parameter uses camelCase (`agentArn`) instead of snake_case
issues.detail: Every other parameter in __init__ is snake_case (aws_access_key, aws_region, etc.) and the rest of the Pipecat codebase follows PEP 8. Exposing `agentArn` as a keyword argument is a permanent public API wart — fix it before the first release. The internal field `self._agentArn` is similarly non-conforming.

issues.description: AWS client is created and torn down on every LLMContextFrame
issues.detail: `async with self._aws_session.client('bedrock-agentcore', ...)` is inside process_frame, so a new aiobotocore client (with full TLS + endpoint discovery handshake) is constructed for every single invocation. In a voice pipeline this adds hundreds of ms of latency per turn and unnecessary load. The client should be created once (e.g., lazily on first use or in a setup hook) and reused, with proper cleanup in cleanup()/close().

issues.description: No exception handling around AgentCore invocation; failures will crash the processor and leave bookends dangling
issues.detail: `client.invoke_agent_runtime(...)`, the async-for over `response['response']`, and `json.loads` in the default response transformer can all raise (ClientError, network errors, malformed JSON). There is no try/except, no ErrorFrame emission, and if an exception fires after LLMFullResponseStartFrame is pushed, the matching End frame is never sent — downstream aggregators will hang. Catch errors, log, push an ErrorFrame, and ensure the response is closed in a finally block.

issues.description: Race condition between timeout-driven End frame and subsequent text frames within the same invocation
issues.detail: _push_text_frame schedules _close_output_response_after_timeout (1s). If the network stalls >1s between SSE parts, the close task fires LLMFullResponseEndFrame, then the next part calls _push_text_frame which opens a *new* response with a fresh Start frame. This produces multiple Start/End pairs for one logical agent response and confuses aggregators. The close timer should only run after the stream completes, not between parts of the same invocation.

issues.description: SSE parsing is too strict and ignores standard event-stream framing
issues.detail: The code splits on '\n' and requires every non-empty line to start with 'data: ', warning otherwise. Real SSE streams contain `event:`, `id:`, `retry:`, comment lines starting with ':', and CRLF line endings. They also use blank-line-separated events with potentially multi-line `data:` fields that should be concatenated. The current parser will spam warnings and drop legitimate frames. Use a proper SSE parser or at minimum tolerate non-data lines silently and split on '\r?\n'.

issues.description: default_response_to_output_transformer can raise json.JSONDecodeError on any non-JSON line
issues.detail: `json.loads(response_line)` will raise on malformed payloads (which agents can easily produce, especially with the over-strict SSE parser above). The function should catch JSONDecodeError and return None, matching the 'Optional[str]' contract documented in the docstring.

issues.description: default_context_to_payload_transformer ignores conversation history and may behave surprisingly when the latest message is from the assistant
issues.detail: Only the very last message is read, and only if its role is 'user' or 'system'. If the assistant just spoke (typical multi-turn voice flow with an OpenAI aggregator that appends assistant messages), the transformer silently returns None and the agent never runs. Either iterate backwards to find the latest user/system message, or document this constraint loudly. Also, the list-content branch joins all `text` parts with spaces, silently dropping non-text parts (images, tool calls) without warning.

issues.description: Credential precedence and region default semantics are surprising
issues.detail: Passing `aws_access_key_id=None` to aioboto3.Session().client() works, but `os.getenv('AWS_REGION', 'us-east-1')` short-circuits boto3's normal region resolution chain (AWS_DEFAULT_REGION, ~/.aws/config, IMDS). Users running on EC2/ECS/Lambda with an instance-role region will be silently overridden to us-east-1. Prefer passing None when nothing was explicitly supplied and let botocore resolve, or document the hardcoded default.

issues.description: No cleanup of pending _close_task on processor shutdown
issues.detail: FrameProcessor has cleanup hooks but this class doesn't override cleanup() to cancel a pending _close_task or close any cached client. If the pipeline tears down mid-response, the close task is orphaned and may push LLMFullResponseEndFrame into a torn-down downstream.

issues.description: `from .agent_core import *` without an __all__ pollutes the aws namespace
issues.detail: agent_core.py defines no __all__, so `import *` re-exports aioboto3, json, asyncio, os, logger, LLMContext, LLMSpecificMessage, OpenAILLMContext, OpenAILLMContextFrame, Frame, etc. into pipecat.services.aws. Add `__all__ = ['AWSAgentCoreProcessor', 'default_context_to_payload_transformer', 'default_response_to_output_transformer']` (or whatever subset is intended).
Use `line.removeprefix('data: ')` or `len('data: ')` to make intent obvious and resilient to typos.
self._last_text_frame_time is assigned but no code consumes it. Either remove the field or wire it into the timeout logic (e.g., to compute remaining sleep). Dead state invites future bugs.

issues.description: No unit tests added for transformers or stream parsing
issues.detail: Both default transformers and the SSE parsing branch are pure-ish and easy to test (mock client response). Given the surface area and the SSE edge cases above, a small test file would meaningfully de-risk the feature.

issues.description: Module docstring references AgentCoreRuntime but parameter is `agentRuntimeArn` — minor inconsistency in naming surface area
issues.detail: The argument passed to invoke_agent_runtime is `agentRuntimeArn` (AWS API name), but the constructor exposes `agentArn`. Either match AWS naming (`agent_runtime_arn`) or rename to `agent_arn`; the current mismatch is confusing.

issues.description: Major boto3/botocore version bump pulled in by aioboto3 15.0 -> 15.5
issues.detail: The lockfile jumps boto3 1.38 -> 1.40 and botocore 1.38 -> 1.40 transitively. Worth flagging in the PR description / changelog since other AWS services in the repo (nova_sonic, sagemaker, etc.) share these deps; a regression sweep against those services before merge is prudent.

dissents.topic: Per-invocation client creation vs cached client

positions.position: Creating a client per LLMContextFrame is a P0 latency bug — voice pipelines budget every ms, and the TLS+endpoint handshake on each turn is unacceptable. Must be cached.

aioboto3 client creation is comparatively cheap and the `async with` block guarantees clean shutdown. Lifecycle management of a long-lived client (cleanup on FrameProcessor teardown, credential refresh) is non-trivial — it's acceptable to ship and optimize later. Treat as P1.

Coupling Start/End to a wall-clock timeout is fundamentally wrong — the stream itself signals completion (async-for ends). The timer machinery should be deleted and bookends emitted strictly around the invocation.

The timeout exists because some downstream consumers want frame-by-frame TTS streaming with sentence boundaries, and the 1s gap heuristic approximates a 'pause'. It's hacky but ships now; revisit when streaming TTS contracts are firmer.
AgentCore agents typically manage their own session/memory server-side, so passing only the latest user prompt is correct and intentional.

Pipecat contexts often have an assistant message appended as the latest entry; returning None silently means the agent never runs in common configurations. Behavior should at minimum search backward for the latest user message.

review.summary: The PR ships a useful integration but has several merge-blocking issues: a public-API naming mismatch (camelCase `agentArn`, plus class name disagreeing with the PR title `AWSBedrockAgentCoreProcessor`), per-frame AWS client creation that will hurt voice latency, and total absence of exception handling around the streaming invocation (which can also leave `LLMFullResponseStartFrame` unmatched). The SSE parser is too strict, the default JSON response transformer can raise on malformed lines, and a timeout-driven End frame can fire mid-stream and cause duplicate Start/End bookends. Smaller but real concerns include missing `__all__` causing wildcard re-export pollution, hardcoded `us-east-1` overriding boto3's region resolution, no cleanup hook for the pending close task, and no tests. The aioboto3 bump also drags boto3/botocore forward by two minor versions across all AWS services in the repo and deserves a regression check.
